records.source: בָּעֵ֨ת הַהִ֜וא אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֣ה אֵלַ֗י פְּסָל־לְךָ֞ שְׁנֵֽי־לֻוחֹ֤תאֲבָנִים֙ כָּרִ֣אשֹׁנִ֔ים וַעֲלֵ֥ה אֵלַ֖י הָהָ֑רָה וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ לְּךָ֖ אֲר֥וֹן עֵֽץ׃
records.gloss: At the time the that said Yahweh to me, cut for yourself two tablets of stones like the first [ones], and come up to me to the mountain, and make for yourself an ark of wood,
pieces: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Cut two stone tablets like the first ones and come up to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on the mountain, and make a wooden ark for yourself,

L.1: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first [ones], and come up to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on the mountain, and make for yourself an ark of wood,

R.1: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Cut two flat stones like the first ones. Come up the mountain to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Also make an ark, a wooden chest.

decisions.choice: at that time: after Moses' forty days of prayer for Israel
decisions.reason: "That time" points back to 9:18-29, where Moses lay before the LORD for forty days and nights and pleaded for the people after the golden calf. The story Moses now tells matches Exodus 34:1-4, where the LORD tells him to cut two new tablets.

decisions.choice: an ark of wood: a wooden chest to hold the tablets
decisions.reason: The word for "ark" means a box or chest; the same word is used for Joseph's coffin (Genesis 50:26). Exodus 25:10-22 and 37:1-9 tell how the ark was made with its gold covering. Moses tells it here briefly, as part of his own story, because the point is that the tablets were kept safe.

decisions.choice: Moses is still speaking: the speech that began at 5:1 continues
decisions.reason: The whole chapter lies inside Moses' long speech (5:1-26:19). The LORD's words that Moses repeats are a speech inside his speech.

decisions.choice: no opening quotation mark; the LORD's words in single quotes
decisions.reason: The double quotation mark that opened Moses' speech at 5:1 stays open until 26:19, so this record has none. Words of the LORD that Moses quotes take single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: a wooden ark / an ark, a wooden chest
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "ark", the name this chest has throughout the Law (Exodus 25:10). Because "ark" today suggests Noah's boat, which is a different Hebrew word, Readable explains it once here as a wooden chest.

records.heading: The two new stone tablets

records.source: וְאֶכְתֹּב֙ עַל־הַלֻּחֹ֔ת אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֛וּ עַל־הַלֻּחֹ֥ת הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר שִׁבַּ֑רְתָּ וְשַׂמְתָּ֖ם בָּאָרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: and I will write on the tablets the words which were on the tablets the first [ones] which you broke, and you will put them in the ark.
pieces: and I will write on these tablets the words that were on the first tablets, the ones you broke. Then put them in the ark.'

L.2: and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke, and you shall put them in the ark.'

R.2: I will write on them the same words that were on the first stones, the ones you broke. Then put the stones in the ark.'

decisions.choice: which you broke: Moses smashed the first tablets when he saw the calf
decisions.reason: Moses told this in 9:17: he threw the tablets down and broke them before the people's eyes (Exodus 32:19). The new tablets carry the very same words; the covenant is renewed, not rewritten.

decisions.choice: I will write: the LORD himself writes the words again
decisions.reason: Moses cuts the stone, but the writing is the LORD's, as with the first tablets (9:10). Verse 4 says that he did so.

decisions.choice: the ark
decisions.reason: As in verse 1: "ark" at every level, explained once in Readable at verse 1.

records.source: וָאַ֤עַשׂ אֲרוֹן֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וָאֶפְסֹ֛ל שְׁנֵי־לֻחֹ֥ת אֲבָנִ֖ים כָּרִאשֹׁנִ֑ים וָאַ֣עַל הָהָ֔רָה וּשְׁנֵ֥י הַלֻּחֹ֖ת בְּיָדִֽי׃
records.gloss: And I made an ark of woods of acacia, and I cut two tablets of stones like the first [ones], and I went up the mountain, and the two tablets [were] in my hand.
pieces: So I made an ark of acacia wood, cut two tablets of stone like the first, and climbed the mountain carrying the two tablets.

L.3: So I made an ark of acacia wood, and cut two tablets of stone like the first [ones], and went up the mountain, and the two tablets [were] in my hand.

R.3: So I built the ark from acacia wood. I cut two flat stones like the first ones. Then I carried the two stones up the mountain.

decisions.choice: acacia: a hard desert tree
decisions.reason: The acacia grows in the dry country of Sinai and the Negev. Its wood is hard and lasts well, and the tabernacle and its furniture were made of it (Exodus 25:10; 26:15).

decisions.choice: I made an ark: told in short, ahead of its place in the story
decisions.reason: Exodus tells of the ark being made after Moses came down (Exodus 37:1). Moses, telling the story years later, puts the ark and the tablets together, because his point is where the tablets were kept. The verb need not mean that he made it before he went up.

decisions.choice: flat stones
decisions.reason: Readable says what the tablets were, flat pieces of stone that could be written on, as in verse 1.

records.source: וַיִּכְתֹּ֨ב עַֽל־הַלֻּחֹ֜ת כַּמִּכְתָּ֣ב הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן אֵ֚ת עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֲלֵיכֶ֥ם בָּהָ֛ר מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֵ֖שׁ בְּי֣וֹם הַקָּהָ֑ל וַיִּתְּנֵ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָֽי׃
records.gloss: And he wrote on the tablets like the writing the first, the ten words which spoke Yahweh to you on the mountain from [the] midst of the fire on [the] day of the assembly, and gave them Yahweh to me.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wrote on the tablets what had been written before: the Ten Words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to you on the mountain out of the fire on the day the assembly gathered. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them to me.

L.4: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wrote on the tablets according to the first writing the ten words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them to me.

R.4: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} wrote on the stones the same words as before. They were the Ten Commandments that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to you from the fire on the mountain, on the day all the people came together. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the stones to me.

decisions.choice: the ten words: the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: "Word" here means a spoken command, a saying. The ten are the commands God spoke to Israel in 5:6-21 (Exodus 20:1-17), and Moses calls them "ten words" in 4:13 as well.

decisions.choice: the day of the assembly: the day Israel gathered at Horeb
decisions.reason: This is the day all Israel stood at the foot of the mountain and heard God's voice out of the fire (4:10-12; 9:10; 18:16).

decisions.choice: to you: the people Moses speaks to were addressed at Horeb
decisions.reason: Most of the people at Horeb had died in the wilderness (2:14-16). Moses still says the LORD spoke "to you", as in 5:2-4: the covenant made there binds every generation as if each had been present.

decisions.choice: the Ten Words / the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "ten words"; Balanced writes "Ten Words" as a name; Readable uses the familiar name, as at Exodus 34:28.

decisions.choice: The LORD wrote
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he wrote"; Readable names the LORD, since "he" could be taken for Moses.

records.source: וָאֵ֗פֶן וָֽאֵרֵד֙ מִן־הָהָ֔ר וָֽאָשִׂם֙ אֶת־הַלֻּחֹ֔ת בָּאָר֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי וַיִּ֣הְיוּ שָׁ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוַּ֖נִי יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I turned and I came down from the mountain, and I put the tablets in the ark which I had made, and they have been there, as commanded me Yahweh.
pieces: Then I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark I had made. They are still there, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded me.

L.5: And I turned and came down from the mountain, and I put the tablets in the ark that I had made, and they are there, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded me.

R.5: Then I went back down the mountain. I put the stones in the ark I had made, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told me to. They are still in it today.

decisions.choice: and they are there: they are still in the ark
decisions.reason: The verb "they were" with "there" describes a state that went on from that day to the day Moses speaks. The tablets were still kept in the ark as Israel stood on the plains of Moab (compare 31:26; 1 Kings 8:9).

decisions.choice: still
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "still" to show that the tablets have stayed there up to the time of speaking.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל נָֽסְע֛וּ מִבְּאֵרֹ֥ת בְּנֵי־יַעֲקָ֖ן מוֹסֵרָ֑ה שָׁ֣ם מֵ֤ת אַהֲרֹן֙ וַיִּקָּבֵ֣ר שָׁ֔ם וַיְכַהֵ֛ן אֶלְעָזָ֥ר בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Israel set out from Beeroth Bene-jaakan [to] Moserah; there died Aaron, and he was buried there, and served as priest Eleazar his son in his place.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set out from Beeroth Bene-jaakan for Moserah. There Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar became priest in his place.

L.6: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel set out from Beeroth Bene-jaakan [to] Moserah. There Aaron died, and there he was buried, and Eleazar his son served as priest in his place.

R.6: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} traveled from the wells of Bene-jaakan to Moserah. Aaron died there and was buried there. Then his son Eleazar became the priest in his place.

decisions.choice: verses 6-9: a note set into Moses' speech
decisions.reason: Moses has been speaking to Israel in the first person ("I", "you"). Here the text speaks of "the sons of Israel" and of Aaron in the third person, a short note about the journey and about the priests and Levites, placed beside the story of the ark. Moses' own words take up again at verse 10. Verses 8-9 may be Moses speaking again, since verse 9 says "your God"; the text has no mark to show where the note ends.

decisions.choice: Beeroth Bene-jaakan, Moserah: camps in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Beeroth Bene-jaakan means "the wells of the sons of Jaakan". Numbers 33:30-33 lists Moseroth, Bene-jaakan, Hor-haggidgad and Jotbathah as camps, in a different order from verses 6-7 here. Neither site is known today.

decisions.choice: there Aaron died: at Moserah
decisions.reason: Numbers 20:22-29 and 33:38 place Aaron's death on Mount Hor. Moserah may be the district in which Mount Hor stood, or the two accounts may describe the same event from different points on the route. The text does not settle which.

decisions.choice: no quotation marks around the note
decisions.reason: The double quotation mark that opened at 5:1 stays open through these verses, because the note sits inside Moses' speech and the speech goes on at verse 10. The note is not given quotation marks of its own.

decisions.choice: the wells of Bene-jaakan
decisions.reason: Readable translates the first part of the name, "Beeroth", which means "wells".

records.source: מִשָּׁ֥ם נָסְע֖וּ הַגֻּדְגֹּ֑דָה וּמִן־הַגֻּדְגֹּ֣דָה יָטְבָ֔תָה אֶ֖רֶץ נַ֥חֲלֵימָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: From there they set out to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah [to] Jotbathah, a land of streams of water.
pieces: From there they set out for Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah for Jotbathah, a land of flowing streams.

L.7: From there they set out to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah [to] Jotbathah, a land of streams of water.

R.7: From there they went on to Gudgodah, and then to Jotbathah. There were streams of water in that land.

decisions.choice: Gudgodah, Jotbathah: camps on the wilderness route
decisions.reason: Gudgodah is probably the Hor-haggidgad of Numbers 33:32-33, and Jotbathah is named in Numbers 33:33-34. Neither site is known today.

decisions.choice: streams of water: valleys with running water
decisions.reason: The word for "stream" names a valley that carries water, often only after rain. In dry country such a place was worth remembering.

records.source: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗וא הִבְדִּ֤יל יְהוָה֙ אֶת־שֵׁ֣בֶט הַלֵּוִ֔י לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֑ה לַעֲמֹד֩ לִפְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה לְשָֽׁרְתוֹ֙ וּלְבָרֵ֣ךְ בִּשְׁמ֔וֹ עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: At the time the that set apart Yahweh [the] tribe of the Levi to carry [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh, to stand before Yahweh to serve him and to bless in his name, until the day the this.
pieces: It was then that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} set the tribe of Levi apart: to carry the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and to bless in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. They do so to this day.

L.8: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and to bless in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, to this day.

R.8: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} chose the tribe of Levi for special work. They were to carry the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s covenant. They were to stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and to bless the people in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. They still do this today.

decisions.choice: at that time: in the days at the mountain
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats the start of verse 1 and ties the choosing of Levi to the time of the ark and the tablets at Horeb. Numbers 3:5-13 and 8:5-22 tell how the Levites were set apart for the LORD's service.

decisions.choice: carry the ark, stand before the LORD, serve him, bless in his name: the work of the tribe
decisions.reason: Carrying the ark was the task of Levites (Numbers 4:15; 31:9). Standing before the LORD, serving him and blessing in his name describe priests (18:5; 21:5), who also came from Levi. The blessing is the one given in Numbers 6:23-27.

decisions.choice: the ark of the LORD's covenant
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the word "ark", which it has already explained in verse 1.

decisions.choice: They do so to this day / They still do this today
decisions.reason: "Until this day" means that the tribe goes on doing this work at the time of writing. Balanced and Readable say so plainly.

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֞ן לֹֽא־הָיָ֧ה לְלֵוִ֛י חֵ֥לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֖ה עִם־אֶחָ֑יו יְהוָה֙ ה֣וּא נַחֲלָת֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Therefore not was to Levi a portion and an inheritance with his brothers; Yahweh he [is] his inheritance, as spoke Yahweh your God to him.
pieces: For this reason Levi has been given no portion of land, no inheritance among his brothers; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is his inheritance, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God promised him.

L.9: Therefore Levi has no portion or inheritance with his brothers; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is his inheritance, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God spoke to him.

R.9: That is why the tribe of Levi did not get any land like the other tribes. Instead, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is their share, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God promised them.

decisions.choice: no portion or inheritance: no share of the land
decisions.reason: When the land was divided, each tribe received its own territory. Levi received none, only towns to live in and the offerings brought to the LORD (18:1-2; Numbers 18:20-24; 35:1-8). "His brothers" are the other tribes.

decisions.choice: the LORD is his inheritance
decisions.reason: Instead of land, Levi has the LORD himself, and lives from what is given to him. The LORD said this to Aaron in Numbers 18:20.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Levi ... their share
decisions.reason: "Levi" here is the tribe, spoken of as one man. Readable says "the tribe of Levi" and uses "their".

records.source: וְאָנֹכִ֞י עָמַ֣דְתִּי בָהָ֗ר כַּיָּמִים֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנִ֔ים אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָ֑יְלָה וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י גַּ֚ם בַּפַּ֣עַם הַהִ֔וא לֹא־אָבָ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה הַשְׁחִיתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And I, I stayed on the mountain like the days the first, forty days and forty nights; and listened Yahweh to me also at the time the that; not was willing Yahweh to destroy you.
pieces: As before, I remained on the mountain for forty days and forty nights, and this time too {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} heard me; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not willing to destroy you.

L.10: And I stayed on the mountain, like the first days, forty days and forty nights, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} listened to me that time also; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was not willing to destroy you.

R.10: Once again I stayed on the mountain for forty days and forty nights. And again {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} listened to me. He did not want to destroy you.

decisions.choice: like the first days: as on the first time Moses was on the mountain
decisions.reason: Moses spent forty days and nights on the mountain when he first received the tablets (9:9) and again when he prayed for the people (9:18, 25). Here he goes back to his own story after the note of verses 6-9.

decisions.choice: And I: Moses stresses his own part
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is written out, which the verb did not need. It brings the story back to Moses himself, the one who stood between God and the people (5:5).

decisions.choice: the LORD listened ... was not willing to destroy you
decisions.reason: The LORD had said he would destroy Israel (9:14). He heard Moses' prayer and chose not to. The verse closes the story that began in 9:7.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י ק֛וּם לֵ֥ךְ לְמַסַּ֖ע לִפְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וְיָבֹ֨אוּ֙ וְיִֽרְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־נִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי לַאֲבֹתָ֖ם לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me, arise, go to journeying before the people, and let them go in and let them take possession of the land which I swore to their fathers to give to them.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Get up and set out at the head of the people, so that they may go in and take possession of the land I swore to their ancestors to give them.'

L.11: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Arise, go on the journey before the people, so that they may go in and take possession of the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.'

R.11: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Get up and go at the front of the people as they travel. They are to go in and take the land that I promised their ancestors I would give them.'

decisions.choice: go to journeying before the people: lead the people on the march
decisions.reason: "Before" here means at the head. Moses is told to lead Israel on from Horeb toward the land (1:6-8).

decisions.choice: I swore to their fathers: the oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: The land was promised by oath to Israel's first fathers (1:8; Genesis 22:16-18; 26:3; 28:13). Even after the calf, the LORD holds to that promise.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "fathers"; Balanced and Readable say "ancestors", which is what the word means here: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and those after them.

decisions.choice: the LORD's words in single quotes
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, the LORD's words inside Moses' speech take single quotation marks.

records.source: וְעַתָּה֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מָ֚ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ שֹׁאֵ֖ל מֵעִמָּ֑ךְ כִּ֣י אִם־לְ֠יִרְאָה אֶת־יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ לָלֶ֤כֶת בְּכָל־דְּרָכָיו֙ וּלְאַהֲבָ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ וְלַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְכָל־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
records.gloss: And now, Israel, what [is] Yahweh your God asking from you, except to fear Yahweh your God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
pieces: And now, Israel, what is it that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God asks of you? Just this: that you fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, follow all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways and love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and that you serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your soul,

L.12: And now, Israel, what is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God asking of you, but to fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to walk in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, and to love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your soul,

R.12: Now, Israel, what does {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God want from you? He wants you to fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and to live the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shows you. He wants you to love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and with all your being.

decisions.choice: what ... but: a question that answers itself
decisions.reason: "What is the LORD asking of you, but ..." is a question that expects the answer that follows, and it runs on into verse 13. After all the people have done (9:7-10:11), the LORD's demand is put simply.

decisions.choice: fear: reverent awe that leads to obedience
decisions.reason: To fear the LORD is to take him seriously as God: to honor him, to trust him and to do what he says (4:10; 6:2, 13). It stands here beside love and service, not against them.

decisions.choice: all your heart and all your soul: the whole person
decisions.reason: The heart is the inner self, the mind and will. The soul (Hebrew *nefesh*) is the living self, one's very life. Together they mean with everything one is, as in 6:5.

decisions.choice: Just this:
decisions.reason: Balanced lets the question stand alone and gives its answer after "Just this", which carries the force of "but" ("except").

decisions.choice: live the way he shows you ... your whole self
decisions.reason: Readable explains "walk in his ways" as a way of living, and says "your whole self" for "soul", since many readers take "soul" to mean only the part of a person that lives on after death.

records.heading: What {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} asks of you

records.source: לִשְׁמֹ֞ר אֶת־מִצְוֺ֤ת יְהוָה֙ וְאֶת־חֻקֹּתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּ֑וֹם לְט֖וֹב לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: to keep [the] commandments of Yahweh and his statutes which I [am] commanding you the day, for good to you?
pieces: and that you keep the commandments and statutes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that I am giving you today, for your own good.

L.13: to keep the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes that I am commanding you today, for your good?

R.13: He wants you to obey the commands and laws of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that I am giving you today. They are for your good.

decisions.choice: commandments and statutes: the whole of the LORD's instruction
decisions.reason: The two words together stand for all that the LORD requires, given through Moses (4:1-2; 6:1-2).

decisions.choice: for your good: the commands serve Israel's life
decisions.reason: The LORD's demands are not a burden laid on Israel for his sake but for theirs, so that it may go well with them (4:40; 5:33; 6:24).

decisions.choice: He wants you to obey
decisions.reason: Readable split the long question of verses 12-13 into statements, so it begins this verse with a new sentence carrying on "He wants you".

records.source: הֵ֚ן לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וּשְׁמֵ֣י הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם הָאָ֖רֶץ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Look, to Yahweh your God [belong] the heavens and [the] heavens of the heavens, the earth and all that [is] in it.
pieces: See, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God owns the heavens, even the highest heavens, along with the earth and all that it holds.

L.14: Look, to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [belong] the heavens and the heavens of the heavens, the earth and all that [is] in it.

R.14: Everything belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God: the sky and the heavens above it, all the way up, and the earth and everything on it.

decisions.choice: the heavens of the heavens: the highest heavens
decisions.reason: Repeating a noun this way gives the highest degree, like "holy of holies". All that is above, however far, is the LORD's (1 Kings 8:27; Psalm 148:4).

decisions.choice: the whole world is the LORD's
decisions.reason: This verse sets up the next: the God who owns everything chose Israel's ancestors out of love alone (verse 15; Exodus 19:5).

decisions.choice: Everything belongs to the LORD your God:
decisions.reason: Readable puts the point first and then lists what "everything" includes. It leaves out "Look", whose force the colon carries.

records.source: רַ֧ק בַּאֲבֹתֶ֛יךָ חָשַׁ֥ק יְהוָ֖ה לְאַהֲבָ֣ה אוֹתָ֑ם וַיִּבְחַ֞ר בְּזַרְעָ֣ם אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם בָּכֶ֛ם מִכָּל־הָעַמִּ֖ים כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּה׃
records.gloss: Only on your fathers set his heart Yahweh, to love them, and he chose their offspring after them, you, from all the peoples, as the day the this.
pieces: Even so, it was your ancestors that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was drawn to in love, and after them {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose their offspring, you, from among all the peoples, as is plain today.

L.15: Yet on your fathers {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} set {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart, to love them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose their offspring after them, you, out of all the peoples, as [it is] this day.

R.15: Even so, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love to your ancestors. And out of all the nations {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose you, their children after them, as you can see today.

decisions.choice: set his heart: was drawn to, loved
decisions.reason: The verb means to be attached to someone, to long for them (21:11; Genesis 34:8). It is used again of God's love for Israel in 7:7.

decisions.choice: only: yet, in spite of this
decisions.reason: The word sets the choice against verse 14. The LORD owns all things, and still he chose these people (7:6-8).

decisions.choice: as this day: as it is now, as you can see
decisions.reason: The phrase points to what is plain at the time of speaking: Israel stands before Moses as the people God chose.

decisions.choice: ancestors ... offspring / children
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers". "Offspring" (literally "seed") stays "offspring" at Balanced and becomes "children" at Readable.

records.source: וּמַלְתֶּ֕ם אֵ֖ת עָרְלַ֣ת לְבַבְכֶ֑ם וְעָ֨רְפְּכֶ֔ם לֹ֥א תַקְשׁ֖וּ עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: And you will circumcise [the] foreskin of your heart, and your neck not you will stiffen again.
pieces: Circumcise your hearts, then, and stop stiffening your necks.

L.16: So circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and do not stiffen your neck any more.

R.16: So circumcise your hearts: open them to God. Stop being stubborn.

decisions.choice: circumcise the foreskin of your heart: remove what closes the heart to God
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of the covenant on the body (Genesis 17:10-14). An "uncircumcised" heart is closed and unwilling to hear (Leviticus 26:41; Jeremiah 4:4; 9:25). The command is to open oneself fully to the LORD, so that the inward life matches the outward sign. In 30:6 the LORD promises that he himself will circumcise their hearts.

decisions.choice: stiffen your neck: be stubborn
decisions.reason: The picture is an ox that stiffens its neck and will not take the yoke. Moses has called Israel "a stiff-necked people" (9:6, 13).

decisions.choice: you will circumcise: a command
decisions.reason: The verb form, joined to what comes before, gives an order that follows from verses 14-15: since the LORD loved and chose you, respond to him.

decisions.choice: circumcise your hearts
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out "foreskin", since "circumcise your hearts" already carries the picture. Literal keeps the full wording.

decisions.choice: open them to God ... Stop being stubborn
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture and adds what it means, and says the meaning of "stiffen your neck" without the picture.

records.source: כִּ֚י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם ה֚וּא אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַאֲדֹנֵ֖י הָאֲדֹנִ֑ים הָאֵ֨ל הַגָּדֹ֤ל הַגִּבֹּר֙ וְהַנּוֹרָ֔א אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹא־יִשָּׂ֣א פָנִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יִקַּ֖ח שֹֽׁחַד׃
records.gloss: For Yahweh your God, he [is] God of the gods and Lord of the lords, the God the great, the mighty and the awesome, who not lifts up face and not takes a bribe,
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is God over all gods and Lord over all lords. He is the great God, mighty and awe-inspiring, who plays no favorites and cannot be moved by a bribe.

L.17: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great God, the mighty and the awesome, who does not lift up a face and does not take a bribe,

R.17: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is greater than every god and every lord. He is the great God. He is strong, and people should stand in awe of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He treats everyone the same, and no one can pay {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to change what is right.

decisions.choice: God of gods and Lord of lords: the highest God, over every power
decisions.reason: Joining a noun to its own plural gives the highest degree, as in verse 14. Whatever beings or powers are called gods or lords, the LORD stands above them all (Psalm 136:2-3).

decisions.choice: awesome: one to be feared
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to fear" (verse 12). God is "awesome" because his power and holiness bring people to awe and dread (7:21).

decisions.choice: lift up a face: show favor to someone
decisions.reason: To lift a person's face was to accept them, to treat them with favor. A judge who did it for the powerful was unjust (1:17; 16:19). God does not.

decisions.choice: lift up a face
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture, explained in the note; Balanced and Readable give its sense.

records.source: עֹשֶׂ֛ה מִשְׁפַּ֥ט יָת֖וֹם וְאַלְמָנָ֑ה וְאֹהֵ֣ב גֵּ֔ר לָ֥תֶת ל֖וֹ לֶ֥חֶם וְשִׂמְלָֽה׃
records.gloss: doing justice [for the] fatherless and widow, and loving [the] sojourner, to give to him food and clothing.
pieces: He sees that orphans and widows get justice, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves the outsider living among you and gives them food and clothing.

L.18: executing justice for the fatherless and the widow, and loving the sojourner, giving him food and clothing.

R.18: He makes sure that children without fathers and women without husbands are treated fairly. He loves outsiders who live among you, and gives them food and clothes.

decisions.choice: the fatherless, the widow, the sojourner: people without protection
decisions.reason: In Israel land and protection came through the family. A child without a father, a woman without a husband and an outsider without land had no one to stand up for them (24:17-21; Exodus 22:20-23). The God above all gods is the one who takes their side.

decisions.choice: doing justice: securing what is right for them
decisions.reason: "Justice" here is the fair judgment and the rights that belong to someone; God sees that the weak receive them.

decisions.choice: food: literally "bread"
decisions.reason: "Bread" often stands for food in general.

decisions.choice: He sees that ... / He makes sure that
decisions.reason: The Hebrew continues the description of God from verse 17 with "doing" and "loving". Balanced and Readable start a new sentence with "He".

decisions.choice: the outsider living among you / outsiders who live among you ... them
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sojourner" and "him". Balanced and Readable say what a sojourner was, as in Leviticus 19:33-34, and use "them", since any outsider, man or woman, is meant.

records.source: וַאֲהַבְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־הַגֵּ֑ר כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And you will love the sojourner, for sojourners you were in [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: You too must love the outsider, since you were outsiders yourselves in the land of Egypt.

L.19: And you shall love the sojourner, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.

R.19: So you must love outsiders too. Remember that you were once outsiders in the land of Egypt.

decisions.choice: you will love the sojourner: Israel must do what God does
decisions.reason: Verse 18 said that God loves the outsider; now Israel is told to love the outsider too. Leviticus 19:34 gives the same command.

decisions.choice: you were sojourners in Egypt: Israel's own past
decisions.reason: Israel lived in Egypt as outsiders and was oppressed there (Exodus 1:11-14; 22:20; 23:9). Remembering it, they are to treat outsiders well.

decisions.choice: you too
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "too" to show the link with verse 18: as God loves the outsider, so must Israel.

decisions.choice: outsider
decisions.reason: As in verse 18 and Leviticus 19:34, Balanced says "outsider" and Readable "outsider" for the sojourner.

records.source: אֶת־יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ תִּירָ֖א אֹת֣וֹ תַעֲבֹ֑ד וּב֣וֹ תִדְבָּ֔ק וּבִשְׁמ֖וֹ תִּשָּׁבֵֽעַ׃
records.gloss: Yahweh your God you will fear; him you will serve, and to him you will cling, and by his name you will swear.
pieces: It is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God you must fear and serve; hold fast to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and swear your oaths by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

L.20: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God you shall fear; {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you shall serve, and to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you shall hold fast, and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name you shall swear.

R.20: Fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and no other, and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Stay close to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. When you make a promise, make it in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

decisions.choice: the LORD ... him ... to him ... by his name: placed first for stress
decisions.reason: Each clause puts the LORD before its verb. The order stresses that it is he, and no other god, whom Israel must fear, serve, cling to and swear by (6:13-14).

decisions.choice: hold fast: cling, stay joined
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a man joined to his wife (Genesis 2:24) and of Ruth clinging to Naomi (Ruth 1:14). It means close, lasting loyalty (11:22; 13:5).

decisions.choice: swear by his name: take oaths in the LORD's name
decisions.reason: An oath called on a god as witness and judge. To swear by the LORD's name is to acknowledge him alone as God.

decisions.choice: and no other
decisions.reason: Readable puts into words the stress the Hebrew word order gives (see the first note).

records.source: ה֥וּא תְהִלָּתְךָ֖ וְה֣וּא אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֣ה אִתְּךָ֗ אֶת־הַגְּדֹלֹ֤ת וְאֶת־הַנּֽוֹרָאֹת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָא֖וּ עֵינֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: He [is] your praise, and he [is] your God, who did with you the great [things] and the awesome [things] these which have seen your eyes.
pieces: He is the one you praise and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is your God. You have seen with your own eyes the great and awe-inspiring deeds {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done for you.

L.21: He is your praise, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things that your eyes have seen.

R.21: He is the one you should praise. He is your God. You have seen with your own eyes the great and amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done for you.

decisions.choice: your praise: the one you praise
alternatives: your pride, the one who brings you renown
decisions.reason: The phrase means that the LORD is the one whom Israel praises. It may also mean that he is Israel's pride, the source of its fame among the nations (26:19; Jeremiah 17:14).

decisions.choice: these great and awesome things: the rescue from Egypt and the wilderness
decisions.reason: The great deeds are the plagues, the crossing of the sea and the care in the wilderness that the people saw for themselves (4:34; 7:19; 11:2-7).

decisions.choice: with your own eyes
decisions.reason: "Your eyes have seen" stresses that the people saw it themselves; Balanced and Readable say "with your own eyes".

records.source: בְּשִׁבְעִ֣ים נֶ֔פֶשׁ יָרְד֥וּ אֲבֹתֶ֖יךָ מִצְרָ֑יְמָהּוְעַתָּ֗ה שָֽׂמְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ כְּכוֹכְבֵ֥י הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם לָרֹֽב׃
records.gloss: With seventy persons went down your fathers to Egypt, and now has made you Yahweh your God like [the] stars of the heavens for multitude.
pieces: Your ancestors were seventy persons when they went down to Egypt, and now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has made you like the stars of the heavens, past counting.

L.22: With seventy persons your fathers went down to Egypt, and now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has made you like the stars of the heavens for multitude.

R.22: When your ancestors went down to Egypt, there were only seventy of them. Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has made you as many as the stars in the sky.

decisions.choice: seventy persons: Jacob's family when it went down to Egypt
decisions.reason: Genesis 46:27 and Exodus 1:5 count Jacob's household that came to Egypt as seventy.

decisions.choice: like the stars of the heavens: the promise to Abraham kept
decisions.reason: The LORD promised Abraham that his offspring would be as many as the stars (Genesis 15:5; 22:17). Moses has already said that this has come true (1:10).

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

decisions.choice: only
decisions.reason: Readable adds "only" to bring out the contrast between seventy people and a nation too many to count.
